sports.h3: National Bank Open under way in Canada
sports.summary: The combined ATP and WTA 1000 events opened in Montreal and Toronto, running August 1 to 13.
body: The 2026 National Bank Open presented by Rogers began August 1 with qualifying, and main-draw play runs from August 2 through August 13. The women's event is at Sobeys Stadium in Toronto and the men's at IGA Stadium in Montreal.
The Canadian hardcourt swing is a key tune-up ahead of the North American summer, with ranking points and momentum on the line before the season's later majors.

sports.h3: Norris wins in Hungary to open title defence
sports.summary: Lando Norris took his first grand prix victory of the season at the Hungaroring, lifting his points tally.
body: Lando Norris claimed victory at the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix over 70 laps of the Hungaroring, the opening win of his title defence. The result moved him to 128 points.
The win came just before Formula 1's summer break, giving Norris and his team momentum to carry into the second half of the championship.

sports.h3: F1 heads into its summer break
sports.summary: With Hungary done, the paddock pauses before the second half of the 2026 season resumes.
body: The Hungarian Grand Prix marked the traditional start of Formula 1's summer shutdown, a mandated break before the championship reconvenes for its run to the finish.
Teams use the pause to regroup and plan upgrades, while the title picture stays open heading into the decisive stretch.

sports.summary: The 71st edition of the Dutch top flight begins this week, running through May 2027.
body: The 2026-27 Eredivisie is scheduled to start on August 7 and conclude on May 23, 2027, opening a fresh domestic campaign as clubs finalise their squads.
The new season reopens the familiar contest between the traditional powers and the chasing pack for European places.

sports.summary: The Rolex SailGP Championship continues its global circuit through late November.
body: The 2026 SailGP Championship, the sixth season, is contested over thirteen sail grands prix at venues around the world, running from January to November.
The high-speed foiling series keeps building its calendar as national teams chase points across the season's international stops.

sports.h3: Canada draws set the North American swing
sports.summary: Main-draw action in Montreal and Toronto gets fully under way this week.
body: After qualifying opened the tournament, the main draws in Montreal and Toronto begin their run through August 13, with top players entering the North American hardcourt stretch.
Results here shape seedings and confidence for the events that follow later in the summer.

sports.summary: Eredivisie sides wrap friendlies and fitness work ahead of the opening weekend.
body: With kickoff days away, Eredivisie clubs are completing pre-season friendlies and conditioning, finalising line-ups and any late transfer business.
The opening fixtures will give the first read on which squads have gelled and which still have work to do.

sports.h3: Title race stays tight after Hungary
sports.summary: Norris's win reshuffled the standings but left the championship fight wide open.
body: Norris's Hungarian victory strengthened his position in the standings without settling the title picture, keeping several drivers in contention as the season pauses.
The second half of the calendar will decide whether his defence gathers pace or the field closes the gap.

consumer-tech.h3: TechRadar's August picks favor OLED and audio
consumer-tech.summary: The month's standout gadgets include Samsung's S95H OLED TV, the Marshall Stanmore IV speaker and the GoPro Mission 1 Pro.
body: TechRadar's August roundup highlighted the Samsung S95H, calling it one of the best OLED TVs it has tested, alongside the Marshall Stanmore IV speaker praised for its bass and amp-inspired look.
The GoPro Mission 1 Pro camera also featured, rounding out a month weighted toward display quality and premium audio rather than radical new categories.

consumer-tech.h3: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 pre-registration closes
consumer-tech.summary: The foldable's sign-up window is ending, with a smaller bonus than last year.
body: Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 pre-registration period is closing, and this year's sign-up bonus is smaller than the one offered previously.
The new Ultra foldable is pitched with a brighter anti-glare screen, a bigger battery and experiential design upgrades as Samsung defends its lead in large foldables.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple hides Siri text-editing tools in macOS 27 beta
consumer-tech.summary: Apple has tucked a suite of Siri-powered AI text-editing features into the latest macOS beta.
body: Apple placed a set of Siri AI text-editing tools inside the macOS 27 beta, an early look at how the company plans to weave generative features deeper into the desktop.
The quiet rollout suggests Apple is testing capabilities ahead of a broader push, keeping expectations measured until a formal release.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple raises iPhone 17 prices in Japan
consumer-tech.summary: Apple officially lifted iPhone 17 pricing in the Japanese market.
body: Apple raised iPhone 17 prices in Japan, adjusting to currency and cost pressures in a major market.
Regional pricing moves like this are watched closely as a signal of how Apple is balancing margins against demand in a competitive smartphone landscape.

consumer-tech.h3: Hisense PX4 Pro brings 200-inch cinema home
consumer-tech.summary: The ultra-short-throw laser projector teased at CES pairs 3,500 lumens with Devialet audio.
body: Hisense's PX4 Pro ultra-short-throw laser projector, first teased at CES 2026, offers 3,500 lumens and Devialet audio, aiming to deliver a 200-inch home cinema experience.
The projector reflects a broader push to make big-screen home viewing brighter and more capable without a dedicated theater room.

consumer-tech.h3: Foldables push brighter screens and bigger batteries
consumer-tech.summary: This year's flagship foldables lean on display and battery upgrades over reinvention.
body: The latest foldables, led by Samsung's Ultra, emphasise brighter anti-glare displays, larger batteries and design refinements rather than dramatic new form factors.
The incremental approach suggests the category is maturing, with makers competing on polish and everyday usability.

consumer-tech.h3: AI features spread across everyday apps
consumer-tech.summary: From Siri editing tools to on-device assistants, generative features keep seeping into mainstream software.
body: The steady arrival of AI text and productivity tools in mainstream operating systems shows how quickly generative features are becoming table stakes rather than novelties.
For users, the payoff is convenience baked into familiar apps, though the pace also raises ongoing questions about privacy and reliability.

consumer-tech.h3: CES 2026 launches still filtering to shelves
consumer-tech.summary: Gadgets teased in January are reaching reviewers and buyers through the summer.
body: Several products first shown at CES 2026, including the Hisense PX4 Pro, are only now reaching testing and availability, a reminder of the long gap between announcement and shelf.
The cadence keeps a steady stream of new hardware arriving even in a quieter part of the tech calendar.
